profile.summary: SiteRM is a phylogenetic model, not a neural network. Given a multiple sequence alignment of a protein family, it fits a separate 21 by 21 amino acid substitution rate matrix for every column of the alignment, with the classical LG rate matrix as a prior. For variant effect prediction it scores a mutant by the log probability of mutating away from the wild-type residue at each site after one unit of evolutionary time, summed over sites. It is distributed inside the CherryML Python package, together with FastCherries, the fast tree estimator that makes the fitting practical.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: SiteRM extends the LG model of amino acid evolution by giving each alignment column its own rate matrix. Fitting runs in two steps: FastCherries estimates the cherries of the tree and the per-site rates from the alignment alone, then CherryML's optimiser estimates a rate matrix per site, regularised towards a prior matrix. The authors use the LG matrix as the prior with regularisation strength 0.5, so half the counts come from pseudocounts, and they treat the gap as a 21st state. A variant is scored as the sum over mutated sites of the log transition probability from the wild-type residue to the mutant residue at evolutionary time t = 1, which makes it an independent-sites model with additive per-site effects conditioned on the wild type.

quotes.text: SiteRM is an extension of the LG model that allows for a *different* rate matrix for each site of the MSA.
FastCherries is a drop-in replacement for FastTree which speeds up the tree estimation step of CherryML by 10-100x.

We trained the SiteRM model on the MSAs provided by the ProteinGym benchmark. Duplicate sequences were removed. We used FastCherries with the LG rate matrix and 20 rate categories to estimate cherries and site rates.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There are no weights: the model is fitted from the alignment each time it is used, so a result is defined by the alignments, the code version and the settings. The settings that matter are the prior rate matrix, the regularisation strength, the number of rate categories, the alphabet used for site rates against the alphabet used for the rate matrices, the evolutionary time, and the number of epochs. The ProteinGym scoring script fixes regularisation strength 0.5, evolutionary time 1.0, the lg.txt prior for tree estimation and lg_with_gaps.txt for regularisation, and device cpu. The package is on PyPI as cherryml, so a result should also name the package version or the commit used.

sections.title: Why an independent-sites model
sections.body: The authors argue that the gain over models that learn interactions between sites comes from conditioning on the wild-type residue, which the competing approaches do not do, and from being able to fit family and site specific matrices on very large alignments without overfitting. The largest alignment they processed had about 454,000 distinct sequences of length 364, which took FastCherries about 1,000 seconds on one CPU core, plus about one second per site for the rate matrices.

quotes.text: We attribute our increased performance to conceptual advances in our probabilistic treatment of evolutionary data and our ability to handle extremely large MSAs.

We attribute the remarkable performance of our independent-sites model to conditioning on the wild-type, which is absent from competing approaches, and to our ability to estimate family- and site-specific rate matrices without overfitting.

run_guide.summary: Install the cherryml package and fit site-specific rate matrices for one alignment with the SiteRM training function.

steps.title: Fit SiteRM on one protein alignment
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from cherryml import learn_site_specific_rate_matrices
from cherryml import io as cherryml_io
from cherryml.utils import get_amino_acids

msa = cherryml_io.read_msa("tests/data/Aln0037_txt-gb_phyml.txt")
res_dict = learn_site_specific_rate_matrices(
    tree=None,
    msa=msa,
    alphabet=get_amino_acids(),
    regularization_rate_matrix=cherryml_io.read_rate_matrix("data/rate_matrices/equ.txt"),
    regularization_strength=0.5,
    alphabet_for_site_rate_estimation=get_amino_acids(),
    rate_matrix_for_site_rate_estimation=cherryml_io.read_rate_matrix("data/rate_matrices/equ.txt"),
    num_epochs=30,
)
print(res_dict["learnt_rate_matrices"].shape)
print(len(res_dict["learnt_site_rates"]))
PY
